rubrics.justification: Mostly consistent with the provided 3AB label and image, correctly identifying an expanded blastocyst and visible ICM, but it overstates features such as a well-formed cavity/preparing to hatch and describes TE more confidently than can be supported from this single image.

Integrates age, ovarian reserve, diagnosis, endometrium, first-cycle status, and lifestyle with embryo quality in a clinically meaningful way, though some links (e.g., male factor implying intact female fertility) are somewhat overstated.

The reasoning is structured and generally logical, with conclusions broadly supported by embryo grade and favorable patient factors; minor issues include conflating implantation with live birth and slightly optimistic interpretation of some factors.

Recommendations are largely consistent with standard IVF practice, especially support for single embryo transfer in a young patient with a good-quality day-5 blastocyst; however, the discussion of PGT-A is incomplete and some prognostic statements are a bit stronger than guideline-based evidence supports.

Provides practical next steps including SET, luteal support, counseling, stress management, and cryopreservation planning, though it lacks some finer clinical nuance such as fresh-vs-frozen contingencies or more detailed future-cycle decision points.
